# Cluster Reference

## How jobs are submitted

`sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh` starts the launcher job. Inside it, Snakemake uses
`snakemake-executor-plugin-slurm` to submit each rule as its own SLURM job.

## Compute sites

Everything specific to a compute site lives in one folder under `profiles/`;
the config names it with `hpcProfile`. The science config and samplesheet do
not change when you move.

| Folder | For |
|--------|-----|
| `profiles/longleaf/` | UNC Longleaf (SLURM) |
| `profiles/slurm-template/` | Any other SLURM cluster: copy and fill in the `<...>` values |
| `profiles/local/` | One machine with no scheduler (a workstation, or an interactive GPU node) |

Each folder has two files:

- `env.sh` — sourced by `ChromSimPipe.sh` and `unlock.sh`; makes `python3`
  (≥ 3.11) and `conda` available (`module load ...`, or
  `source ~/miniforge3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh`).
- `config.yaml` — the Snakemake profile: scheduler, account, partitions, and
  each rule's CPUs / memory / GPU.

To set up a new SLURM cluster:

```bash
cp -r profiles/slurm-template profiles/<cluster>
nano profiles/<cluster>/config.yaml   # account, CPU partition, GPU partition (+ QOS if required)
nano profiles/<cluster>/env.sh        # module loads for python3 and conda
# then in config/ChromSimConfig.yaml:  hpcProfile: 'profiles/<cluster>'
sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh
```

`sinfo -s` lists partitions, `sacctmgr show assoc user=$USER` lists your
accounts, and `module avail` shows the available software. Without editing the
config, `--profile profiles/<cluster>` picks a site for a single run. For
`profiles/local`, start with `bash ChromSimPipe.sh` instead of `sbatch`.

## SLURM account and partition (Longleaf)

All of these are in `profiles/longleaf/config.yaml`:

| Setting | Value | Where |
|---------|-------|-------|
| Account | `rc_dphansti_pi` | `default-resources: slurm_account` |
| Default partition | `general` | `default-resources: slurm_partition` |
| GPU partition | `gpu` | `set-resources: simulateShard` |
| GPU QOS | `gpu_access` | `set-resources: simulateShard` |

## Per-rule resource requests

| Rule | Partition | CPUs | RAM | Wall time | GPU |
|------|-----------|------|-----|-----------|-----|
| `convertHic` | general | 4 | 32 GB | 2 h | — |
| `getMotif` | general | 1 | 1 GB | 15 min | — |
| `orientCTCF` | general | 2 | 16 GB | 1 h | — |
| `validateCTCF` | general | 1 | 4 GB | 15 min | — |
| `simulateShard` | **gpu** | 4 | 60 GB | 12 h | **1** |
| `mergeShards` | general | 4 | 64 GB | 2 h | — |
| `analyzeCondition` | general | 4 | 64 GB | 6 h | — |
| `benchmarkSummary` | general | 1 | 2 GB | 15 min | — |

## Log file locations

| Log | Path |
|-----|------|
| Launcher (main Snakemake process) | `ChromSimPipe-{jobid}.out` |
| Each job's stdout / stderr | `output/logs/{rule}_{wildcards}.out` / `.err` |
| SLURM job logs | `output/logs_slurm/` (`--slurm-logdir` in `ChromSimPipe.sh`) |
| Per-job run time / memory | `output/benchmarks/`, summarised in `output/{runName}_benchmarking.tsv` |

## Conda environments in SLURM jobs

Each rule declares `conda:` with an entry from `condaEnvs` in the config, and
the profile sets `software-deployment-method: conda`. Snakemake activates the
environment inside each job. The site's `env.sh` puts `conda` on the `PATH`
that SLURM jobs inherit.

## Checking queue status

```bash
squeue -u $USER                   # all your jobs
squeue -u $USER -t R              # only running jobs
squeue -j <jobid>                 # specific job
sacct -j <jobid> --format=JobID,State,Elapsed,ExitCode
```

## Cancelling jobs

```bash
scancel <jobid>                   # one job
scancel -u $USER                  # ALL your jobs (careful!)
scancel -u $USER --name <jobname>        # by job name
```

After cancelling, run `bash unlock.sh` before resubmitting.

## Legacy cluster scripts

The standalone SLURM batch scripts from before Snakemake was adopted were
written for the lab's original cluster and now live in `legacy/cluster/`.
They are preserved for reference but should not be used.
`sbatch ChromSimPipe.sh` is the current entry point for everything.
